name: s4_d_mechanism
title: The model follows the state; the readers follow a sentence about it
caption: Panel 1 (exp 14, Oracle Lens's reconstructor at layer 44, 200 items per row): a true 32-token span rebuilt by the reconstructor still separates the classes (probe AUROC), while a statement of the property moves the rebuild 0.03 to 0.10 of the class gap; text written in the language moves it 1.39. Panels 2-3 (exp 15, NLA critic, layer 42): pushing h at 11% of its norm along the class direction moves the model's next token (z against 20 random directions); the statement direction (cos 0.10) does not move the model but is what Oracle Lens and the J-lens follow.

notes: Moved off the slide (computed here): language control, Oracle Lens reconstructor: bullets written in French vs German move the rebuild 1.39 of the gap, the statement '- French language' vs '- German ...' 0.10; the NLA's critic on the fixed statement: table column 0.07, parenthesis −0.05, language 0.72. Pushes are 11% of |h|, z against 20 random directions; 'the model' is its own next-token log-odds (newline for table column, close-paren for parenthesis). Exp 14 numbers use the Oracle Lens reconstructor (ar_ptag_pooled, tag 44) in its whitened output space; the span value is a probe retrained on the rebuilt spans (AUROC), not a gap share. Exp 15 directions are built with the NLA's critic; parenthesis model z is sign-flipped so + = expected. Statement pair (exp 15 NLA): 'The current cell is in the first column of the table' vs the fifth-column version; Oracle Lens pair (exp 14): '- column one' vs '- column five'.
